questions.q: Which pin marks the transversus abdominis?
questions.explain: Transversus abdominis is the innermost of the three flat muscles; its fibers run transversely and its aponeurosis helps form the posterior rectus sheath.

questions.q: Which pin marks the extraperitoneal fat?
questions.explain: Order from the muscles inward: transversalis fascia, extraperitoneal fat, parietal peritoneum.

questions.q: Which pin marks Scarpa's fascia (the membranous layer)?
questions.explain: Scarpa's fascia is the deeper, membranous layer of superficial fascia; Camper's is the fatty layer above it.

questions.q: Which pin marks the linea semilunaris?
questions.explain: The linea semilunaris is the lateral border of each rectus, and like the linea alba it is a hernia weak point.

questions.q: Which pin marks the inguinal ligament?
questions.explain: The inguinal ligament runs from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle: the inferior margin of the external oblique aponeurosis.

questions.q: Which pin marks the deep inguinal ring?
questions.explain: The deep ring is the entrance to the inguinal canal, an opening in the transversalis fascia.

questions.q: Which pin marks the lateral umbilical fold?
questions.explain: The lateral umbilical fold covers the inferior epigastric vessels, so it bleeds if cut.

questions.q: Which pin marks the site of direct inguinal hernias (Hesselbach triangle)?
questions.explain: The medial inguinal fossa (inguinal triangle of Hesselbach) lies between the medial and lateral umbilical folds and is a site of direct hernias.

questions.q: Which pin marks the inferior epigastric artery?
questions.explain: The inferior epigastric artery branches from the external iliac artery and runs deep to the rectus.

questions.q: Which pin marks the quadratus lumborum?
questions.explain: Quadratus lumborum is a flat, square-shaped muscle of the posterior wall from the 12th rib and lumbar transverse processes to the iliac crest.

questions.q: Below the arcuate line, what forms the posterior wall of the rectus sheath?
questions.explain: Below the arcuate line all three aponeuroses pass in front of the rectus, leaving only transversalis fascia behind it.

questions.q: Which flat muscle has fibers running perpendicular to the external oblique, superomedially?
questions.explain: Internal oblique fibers run perpendicular to the external oblique; transversus fibers run straight across.

questions.q: A cirrhotic patient has dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus. Which mechanism explains it?
options: Recanalized fetal umbilical veins draining to superficial epigastric veins
Thrombosis of the inferior epigastric artery
Occlusion of the superior epigastric vein
questions.explain: Caput medusae: reopened (recanalized) fetal umbilical veins in liver failure engorge the superficial epigastric veins.

questions.q: During laparoscopy a trocar tears the inferior epigastric vessels. Which peritoneal fold covers them?
questions.explain: The lateral umbilical folds cover the inferior epigastric vessels and bleed if cut.

questions.q: A hernia exits through the deep inguinal ring and travels through the inguinal canal. What is it?
questions.explain: Indirect inguinal hernias go through the deep ring (lateral inguinal fossa) and along the canal.

questions.q: Which structure is the main occupant of the inguinal canal in males?
questions.explain: Spermatic cord in males, round ligament of the uterus in females.

questions.q: The median umbilical fold covers a fibrous remnant of which structure?
questions.explain: The median umbilical ligament is the remnant of the urachus, joining the apex of the fetal bladder to the umbilicus.

questions.q: The round ligament of the liver in the free edge of the falciform ligament is a remnant of which fetal vessel?
questions.explain: The round ligament (ligamentum teres hepatis) is the fibrous remnant of the umbilical vein.

questions.q: Which nerve supplies the cremaster muscle?
options: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve
questions.explain: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1-L2) passes through the inguinal canal and supplies the cremaster and dartos muscles.

questions.q: After hernia repair a man has numbness of the anterior scrotum and root of the penis. Which nerve is most likely injured?
questions.explain: The ilioinguinal nerve (L1) runs through the inguinal canal and supplies the anterior scrotum and root of the penis.

questions.q: The femoral nerve arises from which spinal levels and supplies the quadriceps?
questions.explain: Femoral nerve L2-L4 (her note: femoral, quads).

questions.q: Which muscle is the primary flexor of the thigh at the hip?
questions.explain: Psoas major and iliacus merge at the lesser trochanter as iliopsoas, the primary hip flexor.

questions.q: Body weight is transmitted from L5 to which structure?
options: Base of the sacrum (superior surface of S1)
questions.explain: Body weight passes from L5 to the base of the sacrum, formed by the superior surface of S1.

questions.q: The umbilicus lies at the level of which vertebra?
questions.explain: Per her surface-anatomy slide the umbilicus is at the level of the L3 vertebra. Textbooks often give the L3-L4 disc; use L3 for this exam.
